clue.text: Drink very quietly over in Syrian city

blocks.note: ale is a drink
pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Someone sips a drink very discreetly while in a city in Syria.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleppo is one of the largest and oldest cities in Syria, in the north of the country.

clue.text: Popular female, exquisite, died in radiation

blocks.note: what is popular is in
standard abbreviation for female
rare can mean exceptionally fine
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A well-loved, beautiful woman died from exposure to radiation.
explanation.definitionFit: Infrared is electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths just longer than visible red light.

clue.text: Whose name aptly reveals what fine literature exploits?

definitions.text: Whose name aptly reveals what fine literature exploits?

blocks.note: surface reading: asking which person has a fitting name
setter's reading: good writing makes use of the value of its vocabulary, and a famous poet's surname splits into exactly that phrase

explanation.surface: A riddle asking whose surname suits a literary life.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the Romantic poet's surname as WORDS WORTH: the value of words, which fine literature exploits.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wordsworth, the English Romantic poet, has a name that literally describes the value of language.

clue.text: Stone head of Oizys and her mother

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: Oizys is the Greek goddess of misery
in Greek myth Oizys is a daughter of Nyx, goddess of night

explanation.surface: A stone carving of a goddess's head, alongside her mother.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on Greek mythology: Nyx, the night, mothered many minor gods including Oizys.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony used as a semi-precious gemstone.

clue.text: Toast Schubert, Brahms and Liszt? Cheers!

indicators.note: rhyming slang for pissed, meaning drunk, and a drunken composer's name gets scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
ta is an informal British thank-you, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A toast is raised to three great composers with a cheery cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' looks like raising a glass to Schubert, but it is bread. 'Brahms and Liszt' is Cockney rhyming slang for pissed (drunk), and two more composers make it hide well.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruschetta is Italian grilled bread rubbed with garlic and oil, essentially a kind of toast.

clue.text: Overly admiring male on bank or boats collectively

blocks.note: he is a male pronoun
a bank, as of switches or keys, is a row
taken as written
shipping is ships considered as a whole

explanation.surface: A man on a riverbank gazes adoringly at passing boats.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship someone as a hero is to admire them excessively and uncritically.

clue.text: African brought up in Manila mostly

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows
in a down entry, brought up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Someone from Africa who was raised largely in the Philippine capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' looks like it trims Manila, but it just supplies more letters for the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: A Somali is a person from Somalia, in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Dutch city there not concerned with old Tory leader

indicators.note: not tells us to go without the following letters

blocks.note: taken as written
re means concerning or about
William Hague led the Conservative Party from 1997 to 2001

explanation.surface: A Dutch city whose people don't care about a former Conservative leader.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hague was leader of Britain's Conservative (Tory) Party; drop RE from THERE to leave THE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hague is the Netherlands' seat of government and home of international courts.

clue.text: Laird needs way to cross Irish county river

blocks.note: a lane is a way or road
County Down is in Northern Ireland
standard abbreviation for river

explanation.walkthrough: County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland; 'way' is a road, here split to hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish landed proprietor, an owner of an estate.

clue.text: Bobby stops ambassador travelling back in time

a bobby is a British police officer

explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is a British policeman; HE stands for His Excellency, how an ambassador is addressed.

clue.text: Bath salts used by dad — this may seem absurd

blocks.note: pa is a familiar word for father
Radox is a British brand of bath salts

explanation.walkthrough: Radox is a well-known British brand of bath salts and bath foam; the order follows dad using it.

clue.text: Male cat in bag — start to hunt bear

the start of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

a tom is a male cat
opening letter of the word

clue.text: Propel boat to Capri periodically

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

clue.text: See 6
Musician knocks poet capturing hearts

indicators.note: capturing means holding something inside

blocks.note: raps are knocks
H is the card abbreviation for hearts
an odist is a writer of odes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocks' looks like criticism of the poet, but it supplies letters; an odist is one who writes odes.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhapsodist is one who performs rhapsodies, originally a reciter of epic poetry, and by extension a player or composer of music.

clue.text: Erotic entertainer seen in Spar with a reindeer

blocks.note: a spar is a pole, as on a ship
Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer

clue.text: Bird's call for service in NYC?

clue.text: Satan went to town spreading message for prodigal?

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb advises against wastefulness, exactly what a spendthrift needs to hear.

clue.text: A pint suitable for the occasion

blocks.note: taken as written
PT is the abbreviation for pint

explanation.surface: A pint of beer is just right for the event.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means fitting or appropriate in the circumstances.

clue.text: French articles, about 500, showing Spooner's need?

taken as written
a worker ant

clue.text: Sustain — hold out in antipodean territory

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Latest news at university: daughter had some food

clue.text: Splendid batter for edible plant part
